sentences: Stochastic packing problems may require probing items before learning which ones are available or useful.
The source measures sparsifier size through containment in a scaled feasibility polytope, rather than simply counting queried items.
It asks whether general integer linear programs admit sparsifiers whose degree is independent of total instance size.
The allowed dependence is on availability and accuracy parameters together with intrinsic structural features of the constraints.
Such a theorem would show when near-optimal solutions can be recovered from a bounded amount of structurally relevant information across much broader packing models.
